SPECIAL FORCES IN THE DOCK - Follow up

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight we link the shock arrest of 12 SANDF soldiers with allegations of a rogue hit squad in the military

Unique Selling Point:
This is a follow up on a story we did which detailed two murders of which they may be charged. We have access to three people who can testify to the events which lead to the 12 SANDF soldiers being arrested last month, June 2025. We produced a story in 2023 called OS Special which gives us the necessary history and evidence to understand the significance of the current court case in the context of past crimes, and have the documents to back it up.

Summary:
In late June, two Special Forces members were arrested and ten more handed themselves over to the police as the Hawks swooped in on the core of a Special Forces unit, led by Commander Sunnybooi Wambi. The sensational trial pits the Hawks against the SANDF's specialist soldiers, and threatens to unravel of a web of secrets protecting SANDF criminality from scrutiny. There are two elements to this - firstly the disappearance of two Ethiopians from the Mall of Africa in 2022, allegedly at the hands of the Special Forces and Wambi, and the murder of the Investigating Officer, Frans Mathipa, who was attempting to discover what had happened. The second part is the torture of a former security operative, Pule Nkomo, who refused to play along with a dirty tricks operation at the Thaba Tshwane Military Base in Pretoria and was then allegedly punished by torture by members of the the Special Forces, and Wambi, on instructions from and with the collaboration of senior military leaders.


Further information:
This investigation spans two years.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel for whistle-blower Pule Nkomo.

Press Release:


Open Secrets Revisited
In 2023, we reported on an elite shadow force allegedly operating above the law in the South African National Defence Force (SANDF). Investigations linked the group to the kidnapping of an Ethiopian man and his bodyguard from the Mall of Africa. The SANDF claimed they were on a training exercise. Then the investigator was shot in the head. Illegal surveillance, torture, even murder: the evidence pointed to a dark underworld in our national defence force. Top brass accused us of fabricating the story. But now, 12 SANDF members are in court on charges of murder, kidnapping and vehicle theft. Will the silence around the alleged rogue special force finally be broken? And what secrets will emerge?
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles


Script:


(VO1) TWELVE MEMBERS OF THE SOUTH AFRICAN NATIONAL DEFENCE FORCE ARE FACING CRIMINAL CHARGES WHICH INCLUDE THE MURDERS OF A SENIOR DETECTIVE AND THE TWO CIVILIANS HE WAS TRYING TO TRACE.

(VO2) IT’S A CASE THAT PITS SOUTH AFRICA’S TOP INVESTIGATORS, THE HAWKS, AGAINST SOME OF THE COUNTRY’S MOST SKILLED SOLDIERS, THE SPECIAL FORCES.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
The Hawks have done a very brave thing and doing the hard yards of an investigation that's led to this prosecution.

(VO3) AND IN THE COURT-ROOM, THE ATMOSPHERE HAS BEEN ELECTRIC.
DURING THE BAIL APPLICATION, NO FILMING WAS ALLOWED.
THE ACCUSED COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED.

GOVAN WHITTLES:
The court room’s packed for the appearance of these Special Forces Members.
In the gallery there are family and friends but also plain-clothe policemen and armed military escorts.

(VO4) THE FIRE POWER ON BOTH SIDES – THE MILITARY AND THE POLICE – SIGNAL THAT THIS IS A HIGH-STAKES GAME.
AND WE KNOW SOME OF THE PLAYERS - AND THEIR BACKGROUNDS.

Sound up from 2023 insert: The investigator Hennie van Vuuren is an anti-corruption activist and researcher rolled into one….

(VO5) TWO YEARS AGO, WE SPOKE TO HENNIE VAN VUUREN, THE DIRECTOR OF AN INVESTIGATIVE NOT-FOR-PROFIT ORGANISATION, ABOUT THEIR PROBE INTO THE MILITARY.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
We had various whistleblowers who approached Open Secrets. Many of them work within the state, and those stories came together to support this, what we've now come to is an understanding of the operation of a torture squad within the South African National Defence Force.

(VO6) VAN VUUREN’s TEAM HAD GATHERED EVIDENCE LINKING MEMBERS OF THE SPECIAL FORCES TO SERIOUS CRIMES, INCLUDING MURDER.
SO WE RETURNED TO OPEN SECRETS, TO ASK ABOUT THESE ELITE SOLDIERS - ONCE KNOWN AS THE RECCES - WHO THEY’VE BEEN TRACKING OVER TIME.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
They have been unleashed by politicians and by people within the military who should be keeping these people in their base. They are there to operate outside the borders of our country. The very fact that they were operating inside the country in the way in which they've done is illegal. Parliament hasn't approved it.

(VO7) SPECIAL FORCES ARE TRAINED FOR HIGH RISK MISSIONS ABROAD.
THIS MADE THEIR PRESENCE IN 2022 IN THE MALL OF AFRICA, IN MIDRAND, JOHANNESBURG PUZZLING - ALL THE MORE SO, AS THEY WERE THEN ACCUSED OF ABDUCTING TWO FOREIGNERS FROM THE PARKING BASEMENT.

GOVAN WHITTLES PTC: In December 2022, an Ethiopian man and his bodyguard disappeared into thin air. One moment he was paying for his parking ticket and the next moment he was gone.

(VO8) FRIENDS OF ABDELLAH ABADIGA AND KADIR ABOTESE SOURCED THE MALL’S CCTV FOOTAGE.
IT SHOWED THE FACES OF THE ALLEGED KIDNAPPERS, AND THE NUMBER PLATES OF THEIR VEHICLES.
WE SPOKE TO ABDURAHIM ABADIGA.
HE’D LED THE SEARCH FOR HIS MISSING BROTHER WHO HAD COME TO SOUTH AFRICA IN 2009 AS A REFUGEE, AND LIVED IN BENONI.

GOVAN WHITTLES: When you saw that footage, what did you think? What did you make of it?

Abdurahim Abadiga
Brother of Abdellah Abadiga
I thought some gangster maybe took him because look there, there they dress civilian clothes. …. driving with, uh, Mercedes Benzes, you know. It's a police that indicate us, no, this is not just a normal gangster. This show us the sign of the South African Special Force.

GW: Who said it was the Special Forces?

AA: It's the police.

(VO9) ABADIGA KNEW HIS BROTHER WAS ACCUSED BY THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT OF FUNDING AN ISLAMIC TERRORIST GROUP.
BUT CLAIMS HE HAD NO IDEA WHAT WAS GOING ON.

ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: After I know that this, this, like highly established, well organized team took him, and I'm worried, you know, it's very scary and disturbing.

(VO10) MONTHS LATER, THE HAWKS PUT VETERAN DETECTIVE, LIEUTENANT- COLONEL FRANS MATHIPA, ON WHAT WAS THEN A MISSING PERSONS CASE.
THE INVESTIGATOR WAS CONFIDENT THEY’D FIND THE TWO MEN.

GOVAN WHITTLES:
Abadiga’s brother Abdurahim grew close to the Hawks investigator.
Their regular meetings kept hope alive.
Until he was suddenly gunned down.

(VO11) WHILE DRIVING, THE DETECTIVE WAS SHOT IN THE HEAD WITH A HIGH VELOCITY WEAPON, FROM A MOVING CAR, SUGGESTING A SKILLED MARKSMAN HAD PULLED THE TRIGGER.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
He was the one who was knocking on their door with a rudimentary process of saying, I just want the cell phone records and the vehicle records, or the movement of vehicles involved in an abduction, It's a very rudimentary tool used in every criminal investigation. He was blocked by the legal affairs unit.

(VO12) IN JULY 2023, THE SANDF HAD GONE TO COURT IN A BID TO CLOSE DOWN MATHIPA’S INVESTIGATION - BUT THEIR APPLICATION WAS DISMISSED.
SHORTLY AFTER THAT, MATHIPA WAS MURDERED.
ABADIGA ATTENDED HIS FUNERAL, BUT WAS ADVISED TO FLEE IMMEDIATELY

ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: The same night, I arrived home, pack up my things, I went to the airport and I left the country.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Was your life in danger?

ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: Yes, if these people can kill the Hawks colonel, then who am I? Like, I'm just someone, you know, little boy, a foreigner. So, I was very much concerned.

(VO13) MATHIPA’S KILLING ON THE N1, OUTSIDE PRETORIA, IN EARLY AUGUST 2023, APPEARED TO DEAL A DEATH BLOW TO THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE TWO MEN.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
We were aware that the Hawks were investigating the matter, and we know that that takes time. But I guess the question kept on coming to forefront of my mind, why is it taking so long? You know, is this potentially going to just be another cold case?

(VO14) BUT THE OPEN SECRETS DOSSIER ALSO INCLUDED A SEPARATE SET OF ALLEGATIONS OF SANDF CRIMINALITY.
A FORMER STATE SECURITY AGENT, PULE NKOMO, SAID HE’D BEEN LURED TO THE PRETORIA MILITARY BASE, THABO TSHWANE, AND PRESSURED TO GET INVOLVED IN A DIRTY TRICKS OPERATION, RELATING TO STOLEN SANDF WEAPONS.
WHEN HE REFUSED, HE WAS DETAINED AND TORTURED.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
Pule Nkomo was a person who approached open secrets with a story. He too, suffered at the hands of the SANDF.and he believes those include members of Special Force who held him captive, detained him illegally, and tortured him.

(VO 15) NKOMO ASKED TO KEEP HIS FACE HIDDEN FOR FEAR OF BEING ATTACKED.
BUT HE CAN IDENTIFY HIMSELF BY NAME, AND HAS TOLD HIS STORY TO THE MILITARY OMBUDSMAN AND THE HAWKS, WHO HAVE INVESTIGATED HIS ALLEGATIONS.
HE WAS SO BADLY TORTURED, HE SAYS, THAT THE SANDF TOOK HIM TO HOSPITAL.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Has your torture been confirmed by the Hawks?


Pule Nkomo
Whistleblower
Yes, because the investigating officer said he got the OB book. The SANDF ambulance that took me from Thaba Tshwane to that Pretoria hospital, it’s recorded there, that a male person, Pule Nkomo, was held there, and even then, ambulance came and pick him up,
brought him back, the officers who were accountable for me to be there.

(VO16) NKOMO CAN IDENTIFY TOP SANDF MEMBERS WHO OVERSAW HIS ORDEAL.
BUT HE SINGLES OUT ONE PERSON IN PARTICULAR, COMMANDER SUNNYBOOI PINNY WAMBI.
HIS FACE WAS CAPTURED ON THE CCTV FOOTAGE AT THE TIME OF THE MALL OF AFRICA ABDUCTION TWO YEARS AGO.


PULE NKOMO: The way he tortured people. It's a, it's a very hard way, it's life and death.
GOVAN WHITTLES: But is he dangerous?
PULE NKOMO: He's dangerous. He’s a heartless kind of a person.

(VO17) WE CAN NOW REPORT THAT WAMBI IS ONE OF THE SPECIAL FORCES MEMBERS, CHARGED NOT ONLY FOR THE ASSASSINATION OF THE HAWKS INVESTIGATOR, BUT ALSO THE MURDER OF THE ETHIOPIANS, ABADIGA AND ABOTESE.
IT’S AN ASTONISHING ABOUT TURN WITHIN THE STATE.
AT THE TIME OF OUR FIRST STORY, THE SANDF DENIED THAT SPECIAL FORCES HAD ABDUCTED THE TWO MEN AT THE MALL, SAYING THEY WERE THERE COINCIDENTALLY, ON A TRAINING MISSION.

Defence Force Presser: Chief of the Defence Force General Rudzani Maphwanya
For the record, there are no military squads in the Defence Force that exist to carry out acts of torture and murder, for whatever reasons.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
I sat here in the same room watching the press conference live on You Tube and kind of get that, you know, sort of, something cold running through your blood in the sense that the bad guys are going to win, you know, if the people that are in charge don't care.

Upsound Pule Nkomo: I reported the matter to the DPCI

(VO18) NKOMO SAYS HE WAS HUNTED DOWN AFTER OUR EXPOSE.

GOVAN WHITTLES: After the story was exposed to the public, was anyone looking for you?
PULE NKOMO: Yes. Member of the Special Force were looking for me….I started receiving calls that they wanted to meet with me. We must sort things out.
GOVAN WHITTLES: Did Sunnybooi Pinny Wambi call you himself?
PULE NKOMO: He called me himself via WhatsApp call
GOVAN WHITTLES: How did you know it was him?
PULE NKOMO: I know the voice. I knew his numbers.

Upsound Pule Nkomo: If I wasn’t moved…

(VO 19) NKOMO CLAIMS THEY CIRCLED THE COMPLEX WHERE HE WAS HIDING.

PULE NKOMO: Where I was staying, I could see their cars out, and I could get their registration numbers. I know they don't just go around looking for people for nothing. They were really coming for me.

(VO20) SO NKOMO MADE A BID FOR FREEDOM.
JUST BEFORE DAWN, HE TOOK AN UBER, AND FLED ACROSS THE BORDER.
FOR EIGHT MONTHS HE FLITTED FROM COUNTRY TO COUNTRY IN AFRICA, LIVING IN THE SHADOWS, UNTIL HE SNUCK HOME.

PULE NKOMO: These people, they damage my life in a way that I can’t describe.

GOVAN WHITTLES: What do you mean - they damaged your life?

PULE NKOMO: I'm having tremors, having problem with my eyes, my kidney, because of the torture.

GOVAN WHITTLES: And on a day-to-day basis, how does it affect you?

PULE NKOMO:I always have to to be careful with everything. I can't find employment because if I try to find employment, they take you for medical checkup and then that's where the problem starts.

(VO21) MEANWHILE, ABDHURAHIM ABADIGA, NOW RESETTLED IN HIS HOMELAND, KEPT IN TOUCH WITH THE HAWKS AS THEY SLOWLY CLOSED IN ON THE ALLEGED KIDNAPPERS OF HIS BROTHER.

Abdurahim Abadiga
Brother of Abdellah Abadiga
If it was only my brother case, you know, maybe you can say, okay, he's a refugee with invalid permit, and maybe nobody care about him but now it's linked with the killing of Frans Mathipa, and I hope they are in a very bad position, so we will know the truth. That is my hope.

(VO22) THE STATE SAYS CCTV FOOTAGE SHOWED A DISTINCTIVE BLACK BMW TRAILING FRANS MATHIPA ON THE N1 SHORTLY BEFORE HE WAS ASSASSINATED.
IT PLACES ACCUSED NUMBER SIX, COMMANDER WAMBI, IN THAT VEHICLE.
THE STATE SAYS THE VEHICLE WAS REGISTERED TO THE SAME SANDF FRONT COMPANY, ACCUSED NUMBER 13, WHICH WAS LINKED TO THE VEHICLES ALLEGEDLY USED IN THE ABDUCTION OF THE ETHIOPIANS MONTHS EARLIER.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
At the moment we know …. of attempts to destroy evidence: the car, that was a black BMW, we believe that was used in the assassination. There was an attempt to try and and effectively write that vehicle off and then claim from insurance.

(VO23)THE STATE ALSO ALLEGES THAT ATTEMPTS HAVE BEEN MADE ON THE LIVES OF MEMBERS OF THE PROSECUTION, AND INVESTIGATORS.
NONETHELESS, THE SANDF IS FUNDING A TOP LEGAL TEAM TO REPRESENT THE TWELVE ACCUSED IN COURT.

Hennie van Vuuren
Director: Open Secrets
The level of support, the kind of solidarity that we're seeing for the Dirty Dozen within the SANDF was quite interesting, by their own fellow soldiers. If anything, these members of the SANDF have brought the institution of the army into disrepute.

(VO24) NKOMO’S STATEMENT ABOUT HIS TORTURE WAS GIVEN BY THE PROSECUTOR AS ONE OF THE REASONS WHY THE COURT SHOULD OPPOSE BAIL FOR THE ACCUSED SOLDIERS.

THE PROSECUTOR CLAIMED THAT, “IT’S IN THEIR DNA TO KILL A THREAT AGAINST THEM.”

YET ON FRIDAY, THE NPA SUFFERED AN EARLY SETBACK AFTER YEARS OF HIGH-RISK INVESTIGATION. THEY LOST THE BAIL HEARING.

Phindi Mjonondwane,
NPA Spokesperson
All 12 members of the South African National Defence Force were granted bail by the Randburg Magistrates Court of 10,000 rands each. And as the NPA, we are disappointed in the outcome. We are of the view that the court's ruling is not legally sound, and hence, as the NPA, we took a decision that we will be appealing the court's ruling.

(VO25) THE DEFENCE ATTORNEYS WERE SATISFIED WITH THE RULING: IT SUGGESTED THE STATE’S CASE WAS NOT AS ROBUST AS IT HAD MADE OUT.

Moshoeshoe Moshoeshoe
Attorney representing Accused 1- 8 and 10-13
We view it still as the court has pronounced that there's weakness in the in the in in the state case.

Manfred Schulte
Attorney representing accused 9
I believe we have a valid defence in respect of all of the charges, and that the state's case, as the court confirmed today, is based on circumstantial evidence.

We have access to three people who can testify to the events which lead to the 12 SANDF soldiers being arrested last month, June 2025. We produced a story in 2023 called OS Special which gives us the necessary history and evidence to understand the significance of the current court case in the context of past crimes, and have the documents to back it up. Summary: In late June, two Special Forces members were arrested and ten more handed themselves over to the police as the Hawks swooped in on the core of a Special Forces unit, led by Commander Sunnybooi Wambi. The sensational trial pits the Hawks against the SANDF's specialist soldiers, and threatens to unravel of a web of secrets protecting SANDF criminality from scrutiny. There are two elements to this - firstly the disappearance of two Ethiopians from the Mall of Africa in 2022, allegedly at the hands of the Special Forces and Wambi, and the murder of the Investigating Officer, Frans Mathipa, who was attempting to discover what had happened. The second part is the torture of a former security operative, Pule Nkomo, who refused to play along with a dirty tricks operation at the Thaba Tshwane Military Base in Pretoria and was then allegedly punished by torture by members of the the Special Forces, and Wambi, on instructions from and with the collaboration of senior military leaders. Further information: This investigation spans two years. Extra Budget Items: Travel for whistle-blower Pule Nkomo. - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 14 July 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Open Secrets Revisited In 2023, we reported on an elite shadow force allegedly operating above the law in the South African National Defence Force (SANDF). Investigations linked the group to the kidnapping of an Ethiopian man and his bodyguard from the Mall of Africa. The SANDF claimed they were on a training exercise. Then the investigator was shot in the head. Illegal surveillance, torture, even murder: the evidence pointed to a dark underworld in our national defence force. Top brass accused us of fabricating the story. But now, 12 SANDF members are in court on charges of murder, kidnapping and vehicle theft. Will the silence around the alleged rogue special force finally be broken? And what secrets will emerge? Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles Script: (VO1) TWELVE MEMBERS OF THE SOUTH AFRICAN NATIONAL DEFENCE FORCE ARE FACING CRIMINAL CHARGES WHICH INCLUDE THE MURDERS OF A SENIOR DETECTIVE AND THE TWO CIVILIANS HE WAS TRYING TO TRACE. (VO2) IT’S A CASE THAT PITS SOUTH AFRICA’S TOP INVESTIGATORS, THE HAWKS, AGAINST SOME OF THE COUNTRY’S MOST SKILLED SOLDIERS, THE SPECIAL FORCES. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets The Hawks have done a very brave thing and doing the hard yards of an investigation that's led to this prosecution. (VO3) AND IN THE COURT-ROOM, THE ATMOSPHERE HAS BEEN ELECTRIC. DURING THE BAIL APPLICATION, NO FILMING WAS ALLOWED. THE ACCUSED COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED. GOVAN WHITTLES: The court room’s packed for the appearance of these Special Forces Members. In the gallery there are family and friends but also plain-clothe policemen and armed military escorts. (VO4) THE FIRE POWER ON BOTH SIDES – THE MILITARY AND THE POLICE – SIGNAL THAT THIS IS A HIGH-STAKES GAME. AND WE KNOW SOME OF THE PLAYERS - AND THEIR BACKGROUNDS. Sound up from 2023 insert: The investigator Hennie van Vuuren is an anti-corruption activist and researcher rolled into one…. (VO5) TWO YEARS AGO, WE SPOKE TO HENNIE VAN VUUREN, THE DIRECTOR OF AN INVESTIGATIVE NOT-FOR-PROFIT ORGANISATION, ABOUT THEIR PROBE INTO THE MILITARY. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets We had various whistleblowers who approached Open Secrets. Many of them work within the state, and those stories came together to support this, what we've now come to is an understanding of the operation of a torture squad within the South African National Defence Force. (VO6) VAN VUUREN’s TEAM HAD GATHERED EVIDENCE LINKING MEMBERS OF THE SPECIAL FORCES TO SERIOUS CRIMES, INCLUDING MURDER. SO WE RETURNED TO OPEN SECRETS, TO ASK ABOUT THESE ELITE SOLDIERS - ONCE KNOWN AS THE RECCES - WHO THEY’VE BEEN TRACKING OVER TIME. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets They have been unleashed by politicians and by people within the military who should be keeping these people in their base. They are there to operate outside the borders of our country. The very fact that they were operating inside the country in the way in which they've done is illegal. Parliament hasn't approved it. (VO7) SPECIAL FORCES ARE TRAINED FOR HIGH RISK MISSIONS ABROAD. THIS MADE THEIR PRESENCE IN 2022 IN THE MALL OF AFRICA, IN MIDRAND, JOHANNESBURG PUZZLING - ALL THE MORE SO, AS THEY WERE THEN ACCUSED OF ABDUCTING TWO FOREIGNERS FROM THE PARKING BASEMENT. GOVAN WHITTLES PTC: In December 2022, an Ethiopian man and his bodyguard disappeared into thin air. One moment he was paying for his parking ticket and the next moment he was gone. (VO8) FRIENDS OF ABDELLAH ABADIGA AND KADIR ABOTESE SOURCED THE MALL’S CCTV FOOTAGE. IT SHOWED THE FACES OF THE ALLEGED KIDNAPPERS, AND THE NUMBER PLATES OF THEIR VEHICLES. WE SPOKE TO ABDURAHIM ABADIGA. HE’D LED THE SEARCH FOR HIS MISSING BROTHER WHO HAD COME TO SOUTH AFRICA IN 2009 AS A REFUGEE, AND LIVED IN BENONI. GOVAN WHITTLES: When you saw that footage, what did you think? What did you make of it? Abdurahim Abadiga Brother of Abdellah Abadiga I thought some gangster maybe took him because look there, there they dress civilian clothes. …. driving with, uh, Mercedes Benzes, you know. It's a police that indicate us, no, this is not just a normal gangster. This show us the sign of the South African Special Force. GW: Who said it was the Special Forces? AA: It's the police. (VO9) ABADIGA KNEW HIS BROTHER WAS ACCUSED BY THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT OF FUNDING AN ISLAMIC TERRORIST GROUP. BUT CLAIMS HE HAD NO IDEA WHAT WAS GOING ON. ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: After I know that this, this, like highly established, well organized team took him, and I'm worried, you know, it's very scary and disturbing. (VO10) MONTHS LATER, THE HAWKS PUT VETERAN DETECTIVE, LIEUTENANT- COLONEL FRANS MATHIPA, ON WHAT WAS THEN A MISSING PERSONS CASE. THE INVESTIGATOR WAS CONFIDENT THEY’D FIND THE TWO MEN. GOVAN WHITTLES: Abadiga’s brother Abdurahim grew close to the Hawks investigator. Their regular meetings kept hope alive. Until he was suddenly gunned down. (VO11) WHILE DRIVING, THE DETECTIVE WAS SHOT IN THE HEAD WITH A HIGH VELOCITY WEAPON, FROM A MOVING CAR, SUGGESTING A SKILLED MARKSMAN HAD PULLED THE TRIGGER. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets He was the one who was knocking on their door with a rudimentary process of saying, I just want the cell phone records and the vehicle records, or the movement of vehicles involved in an abduction, It's a very rudimentary tool used in every criminal investigation. He was blocked by the legal affairs unit. (VO12) IN JULY 2023, THE SANDF HAD GONE TO COURT IN A BID TO CLOSE DOWN MATHIPA’S INVESTIGATION - BUT THEIR APPLICATION WAS DISMISSED. SHORTLY AFTER THAT, MATHIPA WAS MURDERED. ABADIGA ATTENDED HIS FUNERAL, BUT WAS ADVISED TO FLEE IMMEDIATELY ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: The same night, I arrived home, pack up my things, I went to the airport and I left the country. GOVAN WHITTLES: Was your life in danger? ABDURAHAM ABADIGA: Yes, if these people can kill the Hawks colonel, then who am I? Like, I'm just someone, you know, little boy, a foreigner. So, I was very much concerned. (VO13) MATHIPA’S KILLING ON THE N1, OUTSIDE PRETORIA, IN EARLY AUGUST 2023, APPEARED TO DEAL A DEATH BLOW TO THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE TWO MEN. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets We were aware that the Hawks were investigating the matter, and we know that that takes time. But I guess the question kept on coming to forefront of my mind, why is it taking so long? You know, is this potentially going to just be another cold case? (VO14) BUT THE OPEN SECRETS DOSSIER ALSO INCLUDED A SEPARATE SET OF ALLEGATIONS OF SANDF CRIMINALITY. A FORMER STATE SECURITY AGENT, PULE NKOMO, SAID HE’D BEEN LURED TO THE PRETORIA MILITARY BASE, THABO TSHWANE, AND PRESSURED TO GET INVOLVED IN A DIRTY TRICKS OPERATION, RELATING TO STOLEN SANDF WEAPONS. WHEN HE REFUSED, HE WAS DETAINED AND TORTURED. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets Pule Nkomo was a person who approached open secrets with a story. He too, suffered at the hands of the SANDF.and he believes those include members of Special Force who held him captive, detained him illegally, and tortured him. (VO 15) NKOMO ASKED TO KEEP HIS FACE HIDDEN FOR FEAR OF BEING ATTACKED. BUT HE CAN IDENTIFY HIMSELF BY NAME, AND HAS TOLD HIS STORY TO THE MILITARY OMBUDSMAN AND THE HAWKS, WHO HAVE INVESTIGATED HIS ALLEGATIONS. HE WAS SO BADLY TORTURED, HE SAYS, THAT THE SANDF TOOK HIM TO HOSPITAL. GOVAN WHITTLES: Has your torture been confirmed by the Hawks? Pule Nkomo Whistleblower Yes, because the investigating officer said he got the OB book. The SANDF ambulance that took me from Thaba Tshwane to that Pretoria hospital, it’s recorded there, that a male person, Pule Nkomo, was held there, and even then, ambulance came and pick him up, brought him back, the officers who were accountable for me to be there. (VO16) NKOMO CAN IDENTIFY TOP SANDF MEMBERS WHO OVERSAW HIS ORDEAL. BUT HE SINGLES OUT ONE PERSON IN PARTICULAR, COMMANDER SUNNYBOOI PINNY WAMBI. HIS FACE WAS CAPTURED ON THE CCTV FOOTAGE AT THE TIME OF THE MALL OF AFRICA ABDUCTION TWO YEARS AGO. PULE NKOMO: The way he tortured people. It's a, it's a very hard way, it's life and death. GOVAN WHITTLES: But is he dangerous? PULE NKOMO: He's dangerous. He’s a heartless kind of a person. (VO17) WE CAN NOW REPORT THAT WAMBI IS ONE OF THE SPECIAL FORCES MEMBERS, CHARGED NOT ONLY FOR THE ASSASSINATION OF THE HAWKS INVESTIGATOR, BUT ALSO THE MURDER OF THE ETHIOPIANS, ABADIGA AND ABOTESE. IT’S AN ASTONISHING ABOUT TURN WITHIN THE STATE. AT THE TIME OF OUR FIRST STORY, THE SANDF DENIED THAT SPECIAL FORCES HAD ABDUCTED THE TWO MEN AT THE MALL, SAYING THEY WERE THERE COINCIDENTALLY, ON A TRAINING MISSION. Defence Force Presser: Chief of the Defence Force General Rudzani Maphwanya For the record, there are no military squads in the Defence Force that exist to carry out acts of torture and murder, for whatever reasons. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets I sat here in the same room watching the press conference live on You Tube and kind of get that, you know, sort of, something cold running through your blood in the sense that the bad guys are going to win, you know, if the people that are in charge don't care. Upsound Pule Nkomo: I reported the matter to the DPCI (VO18) NKOMO SAYS HE WAS HUNTED DOWN AFTER OUR EXPOSE. GOVAN WHITTLES: After the story was exposed to the public, was anyone looking for you? PULE NKOMO: Yes. Member of the Special Force were looking for me….I started receiving calls that they wanted to meet with me. We must sort things out. GOVAN WHITTLES: Did Sunnybooi Pinny Wambi call you himself? PULE NKOMO: He called me himself via WhatsApp call GOVAN WHITTLES: How did you know it was him? PULE NKOMO: I know the voice. I knew his numbers. Upsound Pule Nkomo: If I wasn’t moved… (VO 19) NKOMO CLAIMS THEY CIRCLED THE COMPLEX WHERE HE WAS HIDING. PULE NKOMO: Where I was staying, I could see their cars out, and I could get their registration numbers. I know they don't just go around looking for people for nothing. They were really coming for me. (VO20) SO NKOMO MADE A BID FOR FREEDOM. JUST BEFORE DAWN, HE TOOK AN UBER, AND FLED ACROSS THE BORDER. FOR EIGHT MONTHS HE FLITTED FROM COUNTRY TO COUNTRY IN AFRICA, LIVING IN THE SHADOWS, UNTIL HE SNUCK HOME. PULE NKOMO: These people, they damage my life in a way that I can’t describe. GOVAN WHITTLES: What do you mean - they damaged your life? PULE NKOMO: I'm having tremors, having problem with my eyes, my kidney, because of the torture. GOVAN WHITTLES: And on a day-to-day basis, how does it affect you? PULE NKOMO:I always have to to be careful with everything. I can't find employment because if I try to find employment, they take you for medical checkup and then that's where the problem starts. (VO21) MEANWHILE, ABDHURAHIM ABADIGA, NOW RESETTLED IN HIS HOMELAND, KEPT IN TOUCH WITH THE HAWKS AS THEY SLOWLY CLOSED IN ON THE ALLEGED KIDNAPPERS OF HIS BROTHER. Abdurahim Abadiga Brother of Abdellah Abadiga If it was only my brother case, you know, maybe you can say, okay, he's a refugee with invalid permit, and maybe nobody care about him but now it's linked with the killing of Frans Mathipa, and I hope they are in a very bad position, so we will know the truth. That is my hope. (VO22) THE STATE SAYS CCTV FOOTAGE SHOWED A DISTINCTIVE BLACK BMW TRAILING FRANS MATHIPA ON THE N1 SHORTLY BEFORE HE WAS ASSASSINATED. IT PLACES ACCUSED NUMBER SIX, COMMANDER WAMBI, IN THAT VEHICLE. THE STATE SAYS THE VEHICLE WAS REGISTERED TO THE SAME SANDF FRONT COMPANY, ACCUSED NUMBER 13, WHICH WAS LINKED TO THE VEHICLES ALLEGEDLY USED IN THE ABDUCTION OF THE ETHIOPIANS MONTHS EARLIER. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets At the moment we know …. of attempts to destroy evidence: the car, that was a black BMW, we believe that was used in the assassination. There was an attempt to try and and effectively write that vehicle off and then claim from insurance. (VO23)THE STATE ALSO ALLEGES THAT ATTEMPTS HAVE BEEN MADE ON THE LIVES OF MEMBERS OF THE PROSECUTION, AND INVESTIGATORS. NONETHELESS, THE SANDF IS FUNDING A TOP LEGAL TEAM TO REPRESENT THE TWELVE ACCUSED IN COURT. Hennie van Vuuren Director: Open Secrets The level of support, the kind of solidarity that we're seeing for the Dirty Dozen within the SANDF was quite interesting, by their own fellow soldiers. If anything, these members of the SANDF have brought the institution of the army into disrepute. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight we link the shock arrest of 12 SANDF soldiers with allegations of a rogue hit squad in the military
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is a follow up on a story we did which detailed two murders of which they may be charged. We have access to three people who can testify to the events which lead to the 12 SANDF soldiers being arrested last month, June 2025. We produced a story in 2023 called OS Special which gives us the necessary history and evidence to understand the significance of the current court case in the context of past crimes, and have the documents to back it up.
metadata.Summary: In late June, two Special Forces members were arrested and ten more handed themselves over to the police as the Hawks swooped in on the core of a Special Forces unit, led by Commander Sunnybooi Wambi. The sensational trial pits the Hawks against the SANDF's specialist soldiers, and threatens to unravel of a web of secrets protecting SANDF criminality from scrutiny. There are two elements to this - firstly the disappearance of two Ethiopians from the Mall of Africa in 2022, allegedly at the hands of the Special Forces and Wambi, and the murder of the Investigating Officer, Frans Mathipa, who was attempting to discover what had happened. The second part is the torture of a former security operative, Pule Nkomo, who refused to play along with a dirty tricks operation at the Thaba Tshwane Military Base in Pretoria and was then allegedly punished by torture by members of the the Special Forces, and Wambi, on instructions from and with the collaboration of senior military leaders.
